description: The individual geometric (GC*) and dimensional (DC*) constraint commands that GEOMCONSTRAINT/DIMCONSTRAINT dispatch to, with the constraint settings, bars and removal commands; then the editing commands that are not in the core Modify chunk - break at point, blend curves, array editing, the command-line CHANGE/CHPROP property editors, hatch boundary regeneration, groups, copy-to-layer, rename - and the Express Tools that extend editing and selection (MOCORO, MSTRETCH, EXTRIM, EXOFFSET, COPYM, SUPERHATCH, CDORDER, MPEDIT, TREX, FS, SSX, GETSEL, DIMREASSOC).

tools.name: GCCOINCIDENT
tools.description: Applies a coincident geometric constraint: forces a point on one object (endpoint, midpoint, centre, insertion) to stay on a point or anywhere along another object, so the two remain connected when either is edited. It is the most common constraint - AUTOCONSTRAIN applies it wherever endpoints already touch - and the Object option constrains a point to lie on a curve rather than at a specific point.
tools.usage:
GCCOINCIDENT
Select first point or [Object/Autoconstrain] <Object>: <hover an object, click the red point glyph>
Select second point or [Object] <Object>: <point or O then pick an object>

parameters.name: Object
parameters.description: Select an object instead of a point; the first point is then constrained to lie anywhere on that object.

parameters.name: Autoconstrain
parameters.description: Apply coincident constraints to all touching points in a selection, like AUTOCONSTRAIN limited to coincidence.

tools.example:
GCCOINCIDENT
(hover the end of line 1, click the endpoint glyph)
(hover the end of line 2, click its endpoint glyph)
-> a blue coincident dot appears at the joint
tools.notes: Constraint glyphs (constraint bars) are shown per CONSTRAINTBAR settings; hover a bar to highlight the objects involved, right-click to delete a single constraint. Constrained points on blocks use the block's insertion point.

tools.name: GCCOLLINEAR
tools.description: Constrains two or more lines (or polyline segments) to lie along the same infinite line. The second object is aligned to the first; with Multiple, every subsequent object is aligned to the first selection. Used for edges that must stay flush when a part is resized.
tools.usage:
GCCOLLINEAR
Select first object or [Multiple]: <line> | M
Select second object: <line>

parameters.name: Multiple
parameters.description: Keep selecting objects to make all collinear with the first.

tools.example:
GCCOLLINEAR
M
(pick the base line)
(pick each step of the profile that must stay flush) Enter
tools.notes: Only linear objects. The first object stays fixed unless it is itself moved by other constraints; add GCFIX to anchor it.

tools.name: GCCONCENTRIC
tools.description: Constrains two arcs, circles or ellipses to share the same centre point. Typical for bolt holes and counterbores, keyways and any nested round feature; combined with a DCRADIUS or DCDIAMETER on each, the pair stays concentric while sizes are driven parametrically.
tools.usage:
GCCONCENTRIC
Select first object: <arc/circle/ellipse>
Select second object: <arc/circle/ellipse>
tools.example:
CIRCLE 0,0 10
CIRCLE 3,2 5
GCCONCENTRIC (pick the big circle, then the small one) -> the small circle jumps to 0,0
tools.notes: The second object moves to the first. Polyline arc segments are accepted; splines are not.

tools.name: GCFIX
tools.description: Locks a point, or a whole object, to its current position in the WCS so that the constraint solver moves other geometry around it. Every constrained sketch needs at least one fixed point (or a fixed object) or the whole assembly can drift when a dimension is changed. The Object option fixes an entire line/curve including its orientation.
tools.usage:
GCFIX
Select point or [Object] <Object>: <point glyph> | O then pick an object

parameters.name: point
parameters.description: Fixes that point only; the object may still rotate about it.

parameters.name: Object
parameters.description: Fixes position and angle of the object.

tools.example:
GCFIX
O
(pick the baseline of the profile)
tools.notes: Fixed constraints are shown with a lock glyph. Over-constraining (e.g. fixing two ends of a line plus a DCLINEAR on it) is rejected with a message.

tools.name: GCPARALLEL
tools.description: Constrains two lines (or linear polyline segments) to remain parallel; the second is rotated to match the first. Angle changes on one propagate to the other, which is how slot walls and drafted sides stay consistent. GCPERPENDICULAR is the 90-degree counterpart with the same prompts.
tools.usage:
GCPARALLEL
Select first object: <line>
Select second object: <line>
GCPERPENDICULAR
Select first object: <line>
Select second object: <line>
tools.example:
GCPARALLEL (pick the top of the slot, then the bottom)
GCPERPENDICULAR (pick the slot side, then the bottom)
tools.notes: Use GCHORIZONTAL/GCVERTICAL instead when the direction must be fixed to the UCS axes rather than relative to another line.

tools.name: GCHORIZONTAL
tools.description: Constrains a line or a pair of points to be horizontal (parallel to the current UCS X axis); GCVERTICAL does the same for the Y axis. With the 2Points option two points on different objects are aligned horizontally, which is the way to keep, for example, two hole centres at the same height.
tools.usage:
GCHORIZONTAL
Select an object or [2Points] <2Points>: <line> | Enter then pick two points
GCVERTICAL
Select an object or [2Points] <2Points>: <line> | Enter then pick two points

parameters.name: object
parameters.description: A line or polyline segment is rotated to horizontal/vertical about its first point.

parameters.name: 2Points
parameters.description: Two points (endpoints, centres...) on any objects are moved to the same Y (horizontal) or X (vertical).

tools.example:
GCHORIZONTAL

(pick the centre of hole A)
(pick the centre of hole B)
tools.notes: AUTOCONSTRAIN applies these automatically to lines within the angular tolerance set in CONSTRAINTSETTINGS. Horizontal/vertical are relative to the UCS current when the constraint was created.

tools.name: GCTANGENT
tools.description: Constrains a curve (arc, circle, ellipse, spline) and a line or another curve to remain tangent, even if they do not currently touch (the solver moves the second object into tangency). It is the constraint behind parametric fillets, belts and cam profiles; GCSMOOTH is the stronger G2 (curvature-continuous) version for splines.
tools.usage:
GCTANGENT
Select first object: <curve or line>
Select second object: <curve or line>
GCSMOOTH
Select first spline curve: <spline>
Select second curve: <spline, line, arc or polyline>

parameters.name: GCSMOOTH
parameters.description: Requires the first object to be a spline and both to share an endpoint (coincident); enforces curvature continuity.

tools.example: GCTANGENT (pick the arc, then the line) -> the line pivots until it is tangent
tools.notes: Tangency is about the objects' infinite geometry; a line may be tangent to a circle without its segment reaching the touch point. CONSTRAINTSETTINGS > AutoConstrain sets the distance tolerance used when AUTOCONSTRAIN infers tangency.

tools.name: GCSYMMETRIC
tools.description: Constrains two objects or two points to be mirror images about a selected symmetry line. Lines become symmetric in angle and position, circles/arcs in centre and radius; the 2Points option makes two points symmetric about the line. Used for symmetric profiles where only one side is dimensioned.
tools.usage:
GCSYMMETRIC
Select first object or [2Points] <2Points>: <object> | Enter for points
Select second object: <object>
Select symmetry line: <line>

parameters.name: 2Points
parameters.description: Constrain two points rather than whole objects.

parameters.name: symmetry line
parameters.description: Any line; it can itself be constrained (e.g. GCVERTICAL + GCFIX).

tools.example:
GCSYMMETRIC
(pick the left flange line)
(pick the right flange line)
(pick the centreline)
tools.notes: Symmetric lines are not forced to equal length unless GCEQUAL is added. Ellipses and splines are not supported.

tools.name: GCEQUAL
tools.description: Constrains two lines/polyline segments to equal length, or two arcs/circles to equal radius; with Multiple, every further object is made equal to the first. Pairs naturally with one dimensional constraint so a single value drives all equal members (e.g. all four sides of a square).
tools.usage:
GCEQUAL
Select first object or [Multiple]: <object> | M
Select second object: <object>

parameters.name: Multiple
parameters.description: Select several objects to equalise to the first.

tools.example:
GCEQUAL
M
(pick one bolt-hole circle)
(pick the other five) Enter
DCRADIUS (dimension one hole) rad1=4.5
tools.notes: Mixing lines and arcs in one GCEQUAL is not allowed. The equal glyph is displayed on each object.

tools.name: DCLINEAR
tools.description: Creates a linear dimensional constraint (horizontal or vertical distance, chosen by drag direction) between two constraint points or on an object; DCHORIZONTAL and DCVERTICAL force the direction. Unlike a dimension, a dimensional constraint drives the geometry: editing its value or expression (d1=100, d2=d1/2) moves the objects. Dynamic constraints display in a fixed style and do not plot; Annotational ones (DCFORM) look like dimensions and plot.
tools.usage:
DCLINEAR
Specify first constraint point or [Object] <Object>: <point> | Enter then pick object
Specify second constraint point: <point>
Specify dimension line location: <point>
Dimension text = 100  (edit the name/value/expression in place, e.g. Width=100)
DCHORIZONTAL / DCVERTICAL: same prompts, fixed orientation

parameters.name: Object
parameters.description: Constrain the length of a line or the distance between an object's endpoints.

parameters.name: name = expression
parameters.description: The in-place editor accepts a name and an expression using other constraints and user parameters: Height=Width*0.5, ang1=45, rad1=sqrt(d1^2+d2^2)/2.

parameters.name: CONSTRAINTNAMEFORMAT
parameters.description: 0 show names, 1 values, 2 name and expression (Width=100).

tools.example:
DCHORIZONTAL
(pick the lower-left corner)
(pick the lower-right corner)
(place the line)
Width=120
DCVERTICAL ... Height=Width/2
tools.notes: Constraint points are the same glyph points as geometric constraints. Values are stored in the drawing's parameters (PARAMETERS palette). Dimensional constraints can be converted from existing associative dimensions with DCCONVERT.

tools.name: DCALIGNED
tools.description: Creates an aligned dimensional constraint - the true distance between two points, between a point and a line, or between two parallel lines - that drives the geometry. It is the parametric equivalent of DIMALIGNED and the right choice for angled edges and offsets between parallel lines.
tools.usage:
DCALIGNED
Specify first constraint point or [Object/Point & line/2Lines] <Object>: <point> | O | P | 2
Specify second constraint point: <point>
Specify dimension line location: <point>
Dimension text = d1 (edit name/value)

parameters.name: Object
parameters.description: Length of a line or polyline segment.

parameters.name: Point & line
parameters.description: Perpendicular distance from a point to a line.

parameters.name: 2Lines
parameters.description: Distance between two parallel lines (they are made parallel if not already).

tools.example:
DCALIGNED
2
(pick the two parallel slot walls)
(place)
SlotWidth=12
tools.notes: Setting a constraint value to 0 for 2Lines makes them collinear; use GCCOLLINEAR instead. Over-constrained input is refused with a message rather than creating conflicting constraints.

tools.name: DCANGULAR
tools.description: Creates an angular dimensional constraint between two lines or polyline segments, or the included angle of an arc, or from three points; the angle value then drives the rotation of the second line. Used for drafted faces, chamfer angles and linkage positions in a constrained sketch.
tools.usage:
DCANGULAR
Select first line or arc or [3Point] <3Point>: <line> | arc | Enter for three points
Select second line: <line>
Specify dimension line location: <point>
Dimension text = ang1

parameters.name: arc
parameters.description: Constrains the arc's included angle.

parameters.name: 3Point
parameters.description: Angle vertex, then two points.

tools.example:
DCANGULAR
(pick the base line)
(pick the drafted side)
(place)
Draft=95
tools.notes: Angles are in the AUNITS format; expressions may use deg-to-rad functions in the Parameters Manager. The quadrant of the angle depends on where the dimension line is placed.

tools.name: DCRADIUS
tools.description: Creates a radius dimensional constraint on an arc or circle (DCDIAMETER the diameter equivalent) that drives the size: change rad1 and the circle resizes about its centre, or bind it to another parameter (rad1=Width/10). Together with GCCONCENTRIC and GCEQUAL this is how hole patterns and fillets are made parametric.
tools.usage:
DCRADIUS
Select arc or circle: <pick>
Specify dimension line location: <point>
Dimension text = rad1
DCDIAMETER
Select arc or circle: <pick>
Specify dimension line location: <point>
Dimension text = dia1
tools.example:
DCDIAMETER
(pick the bore)
(place)
Bore=25
DCRADIUS (pick a fillet) Fillet=Bore/10
tools.notes: A constrained circle whose centre is not fixed or otherwise constrained may move when its radius changes while other constraints are satisfied; fix the centre with GCFIX when that matters.

tools.name: DCCONVERT
tools.description: Converts existing associative dimensions (linear, aligned, angular, radial, diameter) into dimensional constraints of the same type, so a drawing that was dimensioned conventionally becomes parametric without redrawing constraints. The dimension keeps its position and appearance if the current DCFORM is Annotational, or becomes a dynamic constraint glyph otherwise.
tools.usage:
DCCONVERT
Select associative dimensions to convert: <selection> Enter

parameters.name: DCFORM / CCONSTRAINTFORM
parameters.description: Dynamic (0) or Annotational (1) form for the converted constraints.

tools.example:
DCFORM A
DCCONVERT
(select the five plate dimensions) Enter
-> each becomes a driving constraint that still plots as a dimension
tools.notes: Non-associative dimensions (DIMASSOC 1) must first be re-associated with DIMREASSOCIATE. Ordinate, arc-length and jogged dimensions cannot be converted. The reverse (constraint to dimension) is done by deleting the constraint and re-dimensioning.

tools.name: DCFORM
tools.description: Sets whether subsequently created dimensional constraints are Dynamic (fixed-size on-screen glyphs that never plot and show only in the parametric workflow) or Annotational (use the current dimension style, scale with zoom, and plot like normal dimensions). It writes the CCONSTRAINTFORM system variable; existing constraints can be switched individually through the Properties palette (Constraint Form).
tools.usage:
DCFORM
Enter constraint form [Annotational/Dynamic] <Dynamic>:
CCONSTRAINTFORM = 0 (Dynamic) | 1 (Annotational)

parameters.name: Dynamic
parameters.description: Uniform display style, hidden when not needed, does not plot - for design-intent constraints.

parameters.name: Annotational
parameters.description: Behaves as a dimension in the current DIMSTYLE and plots - for constraints that double as documentation.

tools.example:
DCFORM
A
DCLINEAR ... (creates a plottable, style-driven constraint)
tools.notes: Dynamic constraints also hide when the object is not selected if DYNCONSTRAINTDISPLAY / DCDISPLAY says so. Annotational constraints are not the same as annotative objects.

tools.name: DCDISPLAY
tools.description: Shows or hides the dynamic dimensional constraints of selected objects (or all), the constraint counterpart of CONSTRAINTBAR for geometric glyphs. Hidden constraints still drive the geometry; they reappear when the object is selected. The global switch is DYNCONSTRAINTDISPLAY.
tools.usage:
DCDISPLAY
Select objects: <selection or ALL> Enter
Enter an option [Show/Hide] <Show>:
DYNCONSTRAINTDISPLAY = 0 hide all dynamic constraints | 1 show (default)

parameters.name: Show / Hide
parameters.description: Per-object visibility of dynamic dimensional constraints.

tools.example:
DCDISPLAY
ALL

H
tools.notes: Hidden dynamic constraints are listed in the PARAMETERS palette regardless. Annotational constraints are not affected - control them through layers like dimensions.

tools.name: CONSTRAINTSETTINGS
tools.description: Opens the Constraint Settings dialog with three tabs: Geometric (which constraint types show a bar, whether bars appear immediately after applying, bar transparency, and the CONSTRAINTINFER toggle for inferring constraints while drawing), Dimensional (name format Name / Value / Name and Expression, show hidden dynamic constraints for selected objects, show lock icon), and AutoConstrain (priority order of the constraint types AUTOCONSTRAIN applies, tangent/perpendicular objects must share an intersection point, distance and angle tolerances). +CONSTRAINTSETTINGS opens a given tab.
tools.usage:
CONSTRAINTSETTINGS  (Parametric tab > dialog launcher)
+CONSTRAINTSETTINGS  Tab index <0>: 0 Geometric | 1 Dimensional | 2 AutoConstrain

parameters.name: Infer geometric constraints
parameters.description: CONSTRAINTINFER 1: constraints are inferred from object snaps used while drawing (endpoint gives coincident, perpendicular osnap gives perpendicular...).

parameters.name: Constraint bar display settings
parameters.description: Per-type checkboxes; Only display constraint bars for objects in the current plane; transparency 10-90 (CONSTRAINTBARMODE bits).

parameters.name: Dimension name format
parameters.description: CONSTRAINTNAMEFORMAT 0 Name, 1 Value, 2 Name and Expression.

parameters.name: AutoConstrain tab
parameters.description: Order and enable/disable of Coincident, Collinear, Parallel, Perpendicular, Tangent, Concentric, Horizontal, Vertical, Equal; tolerances for distance and angle.

tools.example:
+CONSTRAINTSETTINGS
2
(move Tangent above Parallel, set distance tolerance 0.05, OK)
AUTOCONSTRAIN (select the sketch)
tools.notes: Settings are user settings (registry). CONSTRAINTSOLVEMODE and CONSTRAINTRELAX are the advanced variables for solver behaviour when a constraint cannot be satisfied.

tools.name: CONSTRAINTBAR
tools.description: Shows, hides or resets the geometric constraint bars (the glyph strips listing each object's constraints) for selected objects or for all constrained objects. Hiding bars declutters a sketch without removing constraints; Reset returns bars to their default positions after they have been dragged.
tools.usage:
CONSTRAINTBAR
Select objects or [Showall/Hideall/Reset]: <selection> | S | H | R
Enter an option [Show/Hide/Reset] <Show>:

parameters.name: Showall / Hideall
parameters.description: Apply to every constrained object in the drawing.

parameters.name: Reset
parameters.description: Move bars back next to their objects.

tools.example:
CONSTRAINTBAR
H
(work on the sketch)
CONSTRAINTBAR
S
tools.notes: Bars show only in the current plane when that option is enabled in CONSTRAINTSETTINGS. Individual constraints are removed by right-clicking a bar glyph or with DELCONSTRAINT.

tools.name: DELCONSTRAINT
tools.description: Removes every geometric and dimensional constraint from the selected objects, leaving the geometry exactly where it is. It is the way to 'freeze' a parametric sketch before sending it to someone else, before exploding into blocks, or to clear a tangle of inferred constraints and start again.
tools.usage:
DELCONSTRAINT
Select objects: <selection or ALL> Enter
-> 'n constraints removed'
tools.example:
DELCONSTRAINT
ALL
tools.notes: Dimensional constraints in Annotational form are deleted with their dimension appearance; convert to real dimensions first if they must be kept (re-dimension). Constraints inside block definitions are removed in the Block Editor.

tools.name: CONSTRAINTINFER
tools.description: Infer Constraints: when 1, geometric constraints are created automatically as you draw or edit using object snaps - snapping to an endpoint adds Coincident, to a perpendicular point adds Perpendicular, drawing a horizontal line with polar adds Horizontal, and so on. It makes sketches parametric without explicit GC* commands but quickly over-constrains drawings that were not meant to be parametric, so it is off by default and toggled from the status bar.
tools.usage: CONSTRAINTINFER = 0 (off, default) | 1 (on)

parameters.description: No constraints are inferred; geometry is plain.
Constraints inferred from osnaps and polar/ortho during LINE, PLINE, RECTANG, CIRCLE, ARC, FILLET, CHAMFER, COPY, MOVE and grip edits.

tools.example:
CONSTRAINTINFER 1
RECTANG 0,0 100,50   ; produces a rectangle with coincident, horizontal, vertical and parallel constraints
tools.notes: Registry setting. Remove unwanted inferred constraints with DELCONSTRAINT. Not supported in AutoCAD LT (constraints are display-only there).

tools.name: BREAKATPOINT
tools.description: Breaks a line, arc, open polyline or spline into two objects at a single picked point without removing anything (2021+). It replaces the old BREAK-with-@ trick and the Break at Point ribbon macro with a real, repeatable command that works in scripts and LISP.
tools.usage:
BREAKATPOINT
Select object: <pick>
Specify break point: <point>
tools.example:
BREAKATPOINT
(pick the wall line)
(pick MID of it)

; AutoLISP
(command "_.BREAKATPOINT" ent pt)
tools.notes: Closed objects (circles, closed polylines) cannot be broken at one point - use BREAK with two points. The new object gets the same properties and is added to the Previous selection set.

tools.name: BLEND
tools.description: Creates a spline that joins the free ends of two open curves (lines, arcs, polylines, splines, elliptical arcs, helices) with tangent (G1) or smooth curvature (G2) continuity, the 2D equivalent of a surface blend. The result is a separate spline; use JOIN to merge it with polylines afterwards.
tools.usage:
BLEND
Continuity = Tangent
Select first object or [CONtinuity]: <pick near the end to blend> | CON
Select second object: <pick near its end>
CONtinuity: Enter continuity [Tangent/Smooth] <Tangent>:

parameters.name: Tangent
parameters.description: Degree-3 spline tangent to both curves at the join (G1).

parameters.name: Smooth
parameters.description: Degree-5 spline with matching curvature (G2); it does not pass through the tangent direction exactly but flows smoothly.

tools.example:
BLEND
CON
S
(pick the end of the arc)
(pick the end of the line)
tools.notes: Pick near the ends you want connected; the far ends are ignored. Not available for closed objects. In AutoCAD LT as well.

tools.name: ARRAYEDIT
tools.description: Edits an associative array (rectangular, polar or path) after creation: change counts, spacing, angles, levels and base point, replace the source objects with different ones, or edit the source objects in place (Source option opens an editing state, closed with ARRAYCLOSE). The same options appear on the contextual Array ribbon tab and as multifunctional grips when an array is selected.
tools.usage:
ARRAYEDIT
Select array: <pick>
Rectangular: Enter an option [Source/REPlace/Base point/Rows/Columns/Levels/RESet/eXit] <eXit>:
Polar:       [Source/REPlace/Base point/Items/Angle between/Fill angle/ROWs/Levels/ROTate items/RESet/eXit]
Path:        [Source/REPlace/Method/Base point/Tangent direction/Items/Rows/Levels/Align items/Z direction/RESet/eXit]
ARRAYCLOSE   Save changes to array? [Yes/No] (after Source editing)

parameters.name: Source
parameters.description: Open the source objects for editing; every item updates when ARRAYCLOSE saves.

parameters.name: REPlace
parameters.description: Replace the source objects with a new selection for all items or selected items only.

parameters.name: RESet
parameters.description: Restore erased items and remove per-item overrides.

parameters.name: Method (path)
parameters.description: Divide (items spread along the path) or Measure (fixed spacing).

parameters.name: ARRAYASSOCIATIVITY
parameters.description: Default for new arrays: 1 associative, 0 individual copies.

tools.example:
ARRAYEDIT
(pick the bolt array)
I
8
X

; Replace the source with a different block in all items
ARRAYEDIT (pick) REP (select BOLT_M12 reference) (pick base point) Y X
tools.notes: Only associative arrays can be edited; arrays exploded or created with ARRAYCLASSIC are plain copies. Individual items can be Ctrl-clicked and moved/erased without breaking the array (RESet restores). Arrays are stored as anonymous blocks with an ACAD_ARRAY extension dictionary.

tools.name: ARRAYCLASSIC
tools.description: Opens the legacy Array dialog (rectangular or polar, with counts, offsets, angle, rotate-items and Preview) that ARRAY used before AutoCAD 2012. It creates non-associative copies, which some users prefer for speed and simplicity, and it is the only dialog-based way to create arrays; -ARRAY is the command-line equivalent for scripts.
tools.usage:
ARRAYCLASSIC
(Array dialog: Rectangular Array [Rows, Columns, Row offset, Column offset, Angle of array] or Polar Array [Center point, Method, Total number of items, Angle to fill, Angle between items, Rotate items as copied]; Select objects; Preview; OK)
-ARRAY  Select objects: ... Enter the type of array [Rectangular/Polar] <R>: ...

parameters.name: Rectangular
parameters.description: Rows, columns, offsets (negative to go down/left), angle.

parameters.name: Polar
parameters.description: Centre, number of items, fill angle or angle between, rotate items.

tools.example:
-ARRAY
(select the chair) Enter
P
0,0
6
360
Y
tools.notes: Path arrays are not available here. The resulting objects are independent copies (no ARRAYEDIT). Kept in every release since 2013.

tools.name: CHANGE
tools.description: Legacy but still useful command-line editor: with a change point it relocates the nearest endpoint of lines to that point, moves circle circumferences, repositions text and blocks; with Properties it changes colour, elevation, layer, linetype, linetype scale, lineweight, thickness, transparency, material or annotative state of any objects. Scripts and old macros use it (and CHPROP) because everything is keyword-driven.
tools.usage:
CHANGE  (alias -CH)
Select objects: <selection> Enter
Specify change point or [Properties]: <point> | P
Properties: Enter property to change [Color/Elev/LAyer/LType/ltScale/LWeight/Thickness/TRansparency/Material/Annotative]:

parameters.name: change point (lines)
parameters.description: The endpoint nearest the point moves to it; with ORTHO on all selected lines are made to end at that ortho position - the classic way to align many line ends.

parameters.name: change point (circle / text / block / attdef)
parameters.description: Circle: new radius through the point; Text: new insertion, then prompts for style, height, rotation and text; Block: new insertion and rotation.

parameters.name: Elev
parameters.description: Z elevation of 2D objects (not available through CHPROP).

parameters.name: Properties keywords
parameters.description: Same set as CHPROP; several can be changed in one run, Enter to finish.

tools.example:
; put all selected objects on layer 0 with ByLayer colour
CHANGE
(select) 
P
LA
0
C
BYLAYER


; snap many line ends to a vertical line (ORTHO on)
CHANGE (select lines) (pick point on the target line)
tools.notes: The change point behaviour differs by object type and surprises newcomers; use CHPROP when only properties are intended. CHANGE cannot alter polylines' vertices - use PEDIT or grips.

tools.name: CHPROP
tools.description: Changes general properties of selected objects from the command line - colour, layer, linetype, linetype scale, lineweight, thickness, transparency, material and the annotative flag - without the change-point ambiguity of CHANGE. It is the workhorse for scripts and LISP that need to move objects between layers or force ByLayer properties, and it accepts several property changes in one run.
tools.usage:
CHPROP
Select objects: <selection> Enter
Enter property to change [Color/LAyer/LType/ltScale/LWeight/Thickness/TRansparency/Material/Annotative]: <keyword>
(enter the new value; repeat; Enter to finish)

parameters.name: Color
parameters.description: ACI number, BYLAYER, BYBLOCK, or T for true colour / CO for colour book.

parameters.name: LAyer
parameters.description: Existing layer name (not created).

parameters.name: LType / ltScale / LWeight
parameters.description: Loaded linetype name, per-object linetype scale, lineweight in mm or BYLAYER/BYBLOCK/DEFAULT.

parameters.name: Thickness
parameters.description: Extrusion thickness of 2D objects.

parameters.name: TRansparency
parameters.description: 0-90, BYLAYER or BYBLOCK.

parameters.name: Annotative
parameters.description: Yes/No for objects that support annotative scaling.

tools.example:
; AutoLISP: move every hatch to layer HATCH and make it ByLayer
(setq ss (ssget "_X" '((0 . "HATCH"))))
(command "_.CHPROP" ss "" "_LA" "HATCH" "_C" "BYLAYER" "_LT" "BYLAYER" "")
tools.notes: Objects on locked layers are skipped silently. For xref-dependent layer names the layer must be spelled with the prefix (SITE|WALL). The ActiveX equivalent is setting Layer/Color/Linetype properties on each object; .NET uses Entity.Layer etc.

tools.name: HATCHGENERATEBOUNDARY
tools.description: Creates a closed polyline (or region) around selected hatch objects, recreating the boundary of hatches whose original boundary objects were erased or that came from other systems. HATCHSETBOUNDARY does the reverse - re-associates a hatch with a new boundary selection - and HATCHSETORIGIN moves the pattern origin of existing hatches so tiles align to a chosen point.
tools.usage:
HATCHGENERATEBOUNDARY
Select hatch objects: <selection> Enter  -> a polyline boundary is created for each
HATCHSETBOUNDARY
Select hatch object: <pick>
Select objects to be used for the new boundary: <closed loop> Enter
HATCHSETORIGIN
Select hatch objects: <selection> Enter
Specify origin point: <point>

parameters.name: HPBOUNDRETAIN / HPBOUND
parameters.description: For HATCH itself: whether boundaries are retained on creation (0/1) and as polyline (0) or region (1).

parameters.name: HPORIGIN / HPORIGINMODE
parameters.description: Default origin for new hatches and how it is chosen (current origin, corners of extents, centre).

tools.example:
HATCHGENERATEBOUNDARY
(select the imported hatches) Enter
HATCHSETORIGIN
(select the tile hatch) Enter
(pick the room corner)
tools.notes: Generated boundaries are placed on the current layer and are not associated with the hatch unless HATCHSETBOUNDARY is then run. Hatches with islands generate one polyline per loop.

tools.name: UNGROUP
tools.description: Dissolves a group so its members become independent objects, selected by picking any member or by name; GROUPEDIT adds or removes members and renames a group; CLASSICGROUP opens the legacy Object Grouping dialog that lists all groups with Selectable/Unnamed flags and Highlight. Groups (unlike blocks) keep members editable while allowing one-click selection, and PICKSTYLE or Ctrl+Shift+A toggles whether picking one member selects the whole group.
tools.usage:
UNGROUP
Select group or [Name]: <pick member> | N then Enter group name
GROUPEDIT
Select group or [Name]: <pick>
Enter an option [Add objects/Remove objects/REName]:
CLASSICGROUP  (Object Grouping dialog: Group Name, Description, Selectable, Unnamed, New, Remove, Add, Rename, Re-Order, Explode, Highlight, Include Unnamed)

parameters.name: Name
parameters.description: Choose a named group from a list instead of picking.

parameters.name: PICKSTYLE
parameters.description: 0 no group/hatch-associative selection, 1 group selection, 2 associative hatch selection, 3 both.

parameters.name: GROUPDISPLAYMODE
parameters.description: 0 grips on all members, 1 single grip at the centre, 2 bounding box with single grip when a group is selected.

tools.example:
GROUP (select the furniture set) N SET_A
GROUPEDIT
N
SET_A
A
(select the extra lamp) Enter
UNGROUP N SET_A
tools.notes: Groups are stored in the ACAD_GROUP dictionary and survive copy/paste between drawings (renamed if clashing). Unnamed groups are given *A<n> names. Objects can belong to several groups.

tools.name: COPYTOLAYER
tools.description: Copies selected objects to another layer in one step, either in place (displacement 0) or moved by a base point/second point, and creates the layer if it does not exist. It is the fast route for 'make a demolition copy of these walls on layer A-WALL-DEMO' without COPY followed by CHPROP. -COPYTOLAYER is the command-line form.
tools.usage:
COPYTOLAYER
Select objects to copy: <selection> Enter
Select object on destination layer or [Name] <Name>: <pick an object on the target layer> | Enter then choose from the Copy To Layer dialog
Specify base point or [Displacement/eXit] <eXit>: <point> | D | Enter for in-place copy
-COPYTOLAYER: same prompts, layer name typed

parameters.name: Name
parameters.description: Choose or type the destination layer; a new name creates the layer.

parameters.name: eXit
parameters.description: Copy in place with no displacement.

tools.example:
-COPYTOLAYER
(select the existing walls) Enter
N
A-WALL-DEMO

(objects duplicated on A-WALL-DEMO at the same position)
tools.notes: Copies keep any explicit colour/linetype overrides; run SETBYLAYER afterwards if the new layer should control display. Originally an Express Tool, core since 2007.

tools.name: RENAME
tools.description: Renames named objects - blocks, dimension styles, layers, linetypes, materials, multileader styles, plot styles, text styles, table styles, UCSs, views, viewport configurations, visual styles - through a dialog with wildcards for batch renames (old name pattern -> new name pattern). -RENAME is the command-line form used in standards scripts to convert layer prefixes.
tools.usage:
RENAME  (alias REN)
(Rename dialog: Named Objects list, Items list, Old Name, Rename To)
-RENAME
Enter object type to rename [Block/Dimstyle/LAyer/LType/Material/multileaderstyle/Plotstyle/textStyle/Tablestyle/Ucs/VIew/VPort]: <type>
Enter old <type> name: <name or wildcard>
Enter new <type> name: <name or wildcard>

parameters.name: wildcards
parameters.description: In the dialog, * and ? in both fields rename groups: old 'A-*' to new 'ARCH-*'.

parameters.name: reserved names
parameters.description: Layer 0, DEFPOINTS, linetypes CONTINUOUS/BYLAYER/BYBLOCK, style STANDARD (in some cases) and xref-dependent names cannot be renamed.

tools.example:
-RENAME
LA
WALLS
A-WALL

; wildcard in the dialog: Old Name  X-*   Rename To  XREF-*
tools.notes: Renaming a block updates every reference; renaming a layer updates objects and layer filters but not text strings or scripts that mention it. LAYTRANS is the alternative for mapping many layer names at once with a standards file.

tools.name: MOCORO
tools.description: Express Tool that moves, copies, rotates and scales a selection set in one command session with a shared base point, switching between operations by keyword until you exit. It saves re-selecting objects and re-picking the base point when placing furniture, symbols or details that need several adjustments.
tools.usage:
MOCORO
Select objects: <selection> Enter
Base point: <point>
[Move/Copy/Rotate/Scale/Base/Undo]<eXit>: <keyword>
(each keyword prompts for its own second point / angle / factor)

parameters.name: Move / Copy
parameters.description: Displacement to a second point; Copy leaves the original.

parameters.name: Rotate / Scale
parameters.description: Angle or factor about the base point.

parameters.name: Base
parameters.description: Pick a new base point.

parameters.name: Undo
parameters.description: Reverse the last operation within the session.

tools.example:
MOCORO
(select the desk) Enter
(pick its corner)
R
90
M
(pick the room corner)
tools.notes: The core alternative is the grip menu (hover a grip, choose Move/Rotate/Scale) or the command COPY with its mOde/Array options. Not in AutoCAD LT.

tools.name: MSTRETCH
tools.description: Express Tool that stretches with several crossing windows or crossing polygons at once, so a whole grid of objects can be lengthened in one operation instead of repeating STRETCH for each region. Define all the crossing areas first, then the base point and displacement.
tools.usage:
MSTRETCH
Define crossing windows or crossing polygons...
Options: Crossing Window(CW) or Crossing Polygon(CP)
Specify an option [CP/CW] to define crossing polygon or crossing window: <corner> | CP | CW
(keep defining; Enter to finish)
Specify base point or [Second point]: <point>
Specify second point: <point>

parameters.name: CW / CP
parameters.description: Rectangular crossing window or polygon; objects touched by any of them are stretched.

parameters.name: Remove objects
parameters.description: After the windows are defined you can shift-select to remove objects from the set.

tools.example:
MSTRETCH
(window across the right ends of all rows) (window across the right ends of the column labels) Enter
0,0
@50,0
tools.notes: Objects fully inside a window are moved, as in STRETCH. Not in AutoCAD LT.

tools.name: EXTRIM
tools.description: Express Tool that trims every object crossing a single cutting edge (polyline, line, circle, arc, ellipse, image frame or text) on one side of it, in a single pick: choose the edge, click the side to discard, and everything sticking past the edge on that side is removed. Ideal for cleaning up hatch lines, grid lines or linework around a title block or a wipeout outline.
tools.usage:
EXTRIM
Pick a POLYLINE, LINE, CIRCLE, ARC, ELLIPSE, IMAGE or TEXT for cutting edge...
Select objects: <pick the edge>
Specify the side to trim on: <point>
tools.example:
EXTRIM
(pick the rectangle around the detail)
(click outside the rectangle) -> all lines extending beyond it are trimmed
tools.notes: Objects entirely on the trimmed side are not erased, only the parts crossing the edge are removed; closed shapes (circles) crossing the edge are broken. Works on blocks' geometry only after EXPLODE. Not in LT.

tools.name: EXOFFSET
tools.description: Express Tool: extended OFFSET that can place the result on the current layer or the source layer, offset several objects at once through the same distance, control how polyline gaps are filled (extend, fillet or chamfer) and continue through a point, remembering its options between runs. The core OFFSET later gained Layer and Multiple options (and OFFSETGAPTYPE), but EXOFFSET still offers the combined multi-object workflow.
tools.usage:
EXOFFSET
Specify offset distance or [Through/Options] <1.0>: <distance> | T | O
Select object(s) to offset or [Options]: <selection> Enter
Specify an option to offset or [Options]: <side point> | O
Options: Distance / Layer (Current/Source) / Gaptype (0 extend, 1 fillet, 2 chamfer) / Multiple

parameters.name: Layer
parameters.description: Put offsets on the Current layer or the Source object's layer.

parameters.name: Gaptype
parameters.description: Same as OFFSETGAPTYPE for polyline corners.

parameters.name: Through
parameters.description: Offset through a picked point instead of a distance.

tools.example:
EXOFFSET
O
L
C

250
(select the three wall lines) Enter
(click the inside)
tools.notes: Not in AutoCAD LT. For scripts the core OFFSET with its Layer option is the portable choice.

tools.name: COPYM
tools.description: Express Tool: enhanced COPY with Repeat (place copies at the same displacement repeatedly), Divide (n copies evenly between two points), Measure (copies every d units along a direction) and a dynamic Array mode, all from one base point. The core COPY gained an Array option in 2012, but COPYM's Divide and Measure remain unique for laying out equally spaced copies between two points.
tools.usage:
COPYM
Select objects: <selection> Enter
Base point: <point>
Second point or [Repeat (last)/Divide/Measure/Array (dynamic)/Undo] <exit>: <point> | R | D | M | A | U
Divide: Second point: <end point>  Number of copies: <n>
Measure: Second point: <direction/end>  Distance between copies: <d>

parameters.name: Repeat
parameters.description: Apply the last displacement again (chain copies).

parameters.name: Divide / Measure
parameters.description: Equal count between two points, or fixed spacing along a direction.

parameters.name: Array (dynamic)
parameters.description: Drag to set count and spacing interactively.

tools.example:
COPYM
(select the column symbol) Enter
(pick its centre)
D
(pick the far end of the grid)
7
tools.notes: Not in AutoCAD LT. The core equivalent of Divide is COPY > Array > Fit.

tools.name: SUPERHATCH
tools.description: Express Tool that fills a closed area with a tiled image, block, xref or wipeout instead of a hatch pattern: it inserts the object once, asks for the tile extents, then arrays it and clips it to the boundary, grouping the result. It is the way to make a brick or paving pattern from a block, or fill an area with a photo texture, in 2D drawings.
tools.usage:
SUPERHATCH
(SuperHatch dialog: Image..., Block..., Xref Attach..., Wipeout..., Select existing <object>, Curve error tolerance)
(insert the tile: insertion point, scale, rotation; Is the placement of this BLOCK acceptable? [Yes/No])
Specify block [Extents] First corner <magenta rectangle>: (tile cell size)
Specify an option [Advanced options] <Internal point>: <pick inside the area>

parameters.name: Image / Block / Xref / Wipeout
parameters.description: Source of the tile.

parameters.name: Extents rectangle
parameters.description: Defines the tile cell; overlap or gaps are controlled by making it smaller/larger than the object.

parameters.name: Curve error tolerance
parameters.description: Chord approximation for clipping against curved boundaries.

tools.example:
SUPERHATCH
(Block... PAVER_300, insertion 0,0 scale 1 rotation 0, Yes; accept the extents; click inside the patio outline)
tools.notes: The result is many clipped block references or images in a group - heavy in large areas; consider a custom .pat pattern for line-based fills. Not in LT.

tools.name: CDORDER
tools.description: Express Tool that sets the draw order of selected objects by their colour number: a dialog lists the colours present and lets you sort them so, for example, the heavy black (colour 7) lines draw on top of the light grey (colour 8) ones, optionally moving the objects to the front or the back of the whole space. Useful for pen-plot style drawings where colour equals pen weight.
tools.usage:
CDORDER
Select objects: <selection> Enter
(Draw Order by Color dialog: list of colours with Move Up / Move Down, Draw order location: Front / Back, Handle objects on layer... options)

parameters.name: colour order
parameters.description: Top of the list draws first (at the back) or last depending on the Front/Back setting.

parameters.name: Front / Back
parameters.description: Whether the reordered objects are placed in front of or behind unselected objects.

tools.example:
CDORDER
(select the whole plan) Enter
(order: 8, 9, 251, 7 with 7 last; Front; OK)
tools.notes: Draw order is stored in the SortEnts table and applies to plotting. The core DRAWORDER works per selection, not by colour. Not in LT.

tools.name: MPEDIT
tools.description: Express Tool: PEDIT for many polylines at once - open, close, decurve, fit, spline, set a global width or linetype generation on a whole selection, and convert selected lines and arcs to polylines in the same pass. The core PEDIT accepts multiple objects too (Multiple option) but MPEDIT's prompt flow is shorter for scripts.
tools.usage:
MPEDIT
Select objects: <selection> Enter
Convert Lines and Arcs to polylines? [Yes/No] <Yes>:
Enter an option [Open/Close/Decurve/Fit/Ltype gen/Spline/Width/eXit] <eXit>:

parameters.name: Width
parameters.description: Set the same constant width on all selected polylines.

parameters.name: Ltype gen
parameters.description: ON makes non-continuous linetypes flow across vertices (PLINEGEN).

parameters.name: Convert
parameters.description: Lines and arcs in the selection become single-segment polylines first.

tools.example:
MPEDIT
(select the contour lines) Enter
Y
W
0.35
X
tools.notes: Joining is not offered here; use PEDIT > Multiple > Join. Not in LT.

tools.name: TREX
tools.description: Express Tool that combines TRIM and EXTEND: pick the cutting/boundary edges once, then click objects to trim and Shift-click objects to extend against the same edges, without restarting the command. The core TRIM/EXTEND adopted Shift-toggle behaviour in 2007 and Quick mode in 2021, so TREX matters mainly in legacy macros.
tools.usage:
TREX
Select cutting edges or boundary edges...
Select objects: <edges> Enter
Select object to trim or shift-select to extend or [Fence/Crossing/Project/Edge/eRase/Undo]: <pick>

parameters.name: Fence / Crossing
parameters.description: Select many objects to trim with a fence line or crossing window.

parameters.name: Project / Edge
parameters.description: Projection mode and implied edge extension, as in TRIM.

tools.example:
TREX
(select the two wall lines) Enter
(click the lines that overshoot; Shift-click those that fall short)
tools.notes: Not in AutoCAD LT; TRIM with TRIMEXTENDMODE 1 (Quick mode) covers the same needs interactively.

tools.name: FS
tools.description: Fast Select, an Express Tool that builds a selection set of every object touching a picked object (and optionally chaining through objects that touch those), which is how a whole connected run of pipes, ducts or wall lines is grabbed with one click. The set becomes the Previous selection for the next command.
tools.usage:
FS
Select touching object or [Options]: <pick> | O
Options: Chain selection [Yes/No], Object types to consider

parameters.name: Chain
parameters.description: Yes keeps adding objects that touch the ones already found until nothing new is reached.

parameters.name: Object types
parameters.description: Restrict the search to certain entity types.

tools.example:
FS
O
(Chain: Yes)
(pick one segment of the pipe run)
MOVE
P
tools.notes: Touching means geometric intersection or shared endpoint; near misses are ignored. Not in LT.

tools.name: SSX
tools.description: Express Tool that creates a selection set from a filter built on a picked object's properties - entity type, block name, colour, layer, linetype, style, thickness, extrusion vector or flags - each of which can be kept, edited or dropped before the set is built. It is the command-line ancestor of SELECTSIMILAR and QSELECT and still handy inside macros because the result is available as Previous.
tools.usage:
SSX
Select object/<None>: <pick> | Enter
>>Block name/Color/Entity/Flag/LAyer/LType/Pick/Style/Thickness/Vector: <keyword to edit that filter> | Enter to build the set
(Each keyword prompts for a value; * removes the filter)

parameters.name: Pick
parameters.description: Restrict to objects picked interactively as well.

parameters.name: Entity
parameters.description: DXF entity type name such as LINE, INSERT, TEXT.

parameters.name: Flag
parameters.description: DXF group 70 flag value (e.g. closed polylines).

tools.example:
SSX
(pick a block reference)
LA
*

ERASE
P
tools.notes: The filter values default to those of the picked object. Not in LT. In LISP, (ssget "_X" filter) is the direct equivalent.

tools.name: GETSEL
tools.description: Express Tool that creates a selection set of all objects on a layer and/or of an object type by picking an example of each, storing it as the Previous set for the following command. Faster than QSELECT for the common 'everything of this kind on this layer' case and scriptable because the answers are single picks or Enter for wildcard.
tools.usage:
GETSEL
Select an object on the Source layer <*>: <pick> | Enter for any layer
Select an object of the Type you want <*>: <pick> | Enter for any type
-> 'Collected n objects'
tools.example:
GETSEL
(pick a text on layer NOTES)
(pick a text)
SCALETEXT
P

E
P
2.5
tools.notes: Includes objects in frozen/locked layers in the count but they may not be editable. Not in LT.

tools.name: DIMREASSOC
tools.description: Express Tool that restores the true measured value to dimensions whose text was overridden or edited (e.g. someone typed 100 over a 98.5 measurement). It clears the text override on each selected dimension so the value updates again with the geometry - the standard audit step before issuing drawings. Not to be confused with the core DIMREASSOCIATE, which re-links dimensions to geometry.
tools.usage:
DIMREASSOC
Select objects: <dimensions> Enter
-> reports the number of dimensions whose text was reset
tools.example:
DIMREASSOC
ALL
tools.notes: Overrides that include the <> placeholder (prefix/suffix around the measurement) are also reset to plain measurement. Not in LT; the core way is DIMEDIT N with <> or clearing Text override in Properties.
